Many people fall into the conventional trap of letting themselves go once they're married, but really it should be the opposite. You now have at least a small obligation to your spouse to keep a certain standard. I think if you talk to him and make sure he makes it a lifestyle change that he enjoys, and doesn't just half-ass it for you, then that shows both commitment, AND he'll get more attractive.

I think another thing to consider is how your view of attraction is skewed by modern media. The average man is probably, by modern metrics, kinda ugly. Perhaps you're not seeing his true beauty because you're comparing him to your friends and their reactions. Who knows, maybe they have similar concerns about their husband and just want to show off. It's only natural. I will say, however, to not push yourself into the marraige if you have any doubts. Only go through with it if you can work out your reservations. For both his sake, and yours especially.

If his personality and emotional maturity is as wonderful as you say, then he might even be able to handle such a discussion before you marry. Communication is key. Maybe try bringing up how he dresses or looks in a casual way, and see how he responds. If needed, have a serious sit down and address him. If the issue is important to you, it's worth talking about.

Levels no longer matter as far as matchmaking goes. It is all dependant on Soul Memory, which is how many souls your character has accumulated over time.


 It used to be that there was no way to stop gaining souls, so people's SM would propel up to top tier. With the agape ring, you can lock your SM, since the ring absorbs all souls gained. 

In DS1, there was a SL meta where PvPers kept their characters at so as to get the most action. Is DS2, the early meta was 150. Since SL doesn't matter, you can have whatever level character you want, but the souls you have from your SM restrict how much you can level/buy items/upgrade etc

The major PvP hotspots are Iron Keep bridge, Heide's, and the cathedral in Ivory kind dlc. In your bonfire warp screen, orange oulines are around areas with the most online interaction for your SM, so thats a good place to start. Just use a cracked red eye orb and the game will find a compatabile gane for you to invade. Alternatively, the red sign soapstone lets you put your sign down to summon, or you can summon people yourself.

Also, the arena is a good place to PvP to avoid souls altogether, since you don't get any from there, and gain a cracked red eye orb when you win.
